Job Description

Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Networking is the foundation that enables customers to run mission-critical workloads at global cloud scale.

We're rearchitecting OCI's physical network control and management systems from the ground up to support the next generation of networking services. This is a unique opportunity to influence the architecture of one of the world's largest cloud networking platforms. We're looking for experienced leaders with proven record of building and operating large-scale distributed systems, deep understanding of distributed orchestration services, and a passion for growing high-performant teams to join our leadership team.

Our team develops the core infrastructure that powers OCI Networking's control plane, solving complex challenges in managing network configuration at cloud scale. You'll collaborate across OCI Networking and Infrastructure teams to shape the future of OCI Networking.

Responsibilities

As a Director of Software Engineering, you will lead teams that design, develop, deploy, and operate highly available, large-scale distributed services for Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Networking. You will apply your engineering leadership experience and knowledge of software architecture to deliver critical infrastructure that powers OCI Networking’s control and management systems.

Lead and develop software engineering teams through engineering managers and technical leads.
Drive execution of technical and organizational priorities, ensuring delivery of reliable, scalable, and operable services.
Partner with teams across OCI Networking to design and deliver large-scale cloud infrastructure.
Establish strong engineering practices and operational excellence for production distributed systems.
Deliver complex projects on time with high quality while effectively managing dependencies, risks, and priorities.
Develop engineering leaders and create an environment that supports technical excellence, collaboration, and growth.

You should value simplicity and scale, thrive in a collaborative environment, and enjoy solving challenging distributed systems and cloud networking problems.

8+ years of experience leading engineering teams building and operating highly available, production-grade distributed systems or cloud infrastructure.
Experience managing engineering managers and/or senior technical leaders.
Strong understanding of distributed systems and software architecture.
Familiarity with networking fundamentals and configuration management is highly desirable.
Experience with modern software development and deployment practices, including CI/CD pipelines, release automation, and large-scale deployment workflows.
Demonstrated ability to deliver complex engineering initiatives and collaborate effectively across organizational boundaries.
BS or MS in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

jobs.description:
Build the future, spark innovation and align your career with purpose.

McKinstry is innovating the waste and climate harm out of the built environment and creating lasting impact. Together, we’re building a thriving planet.

Buildings are a leading contributor to the climate crisis, generating nearly 40% of total global energy-related carbon emissions. We’re making a lasting impact on our industry and within our communities by addressing the climate, affordability and equity crises through:

renewables and energy services
engineering and design
construction and facility services

To get where we’re going, we need big thinkers, problem solvers and collaborative mindsets. Does that sound like you?

The Opportunity with McKinstry

We are adding a Director, AI Engineering
to our team in Seattle, WA. The Director, AI Engineering owns the development of the company’s core AI technology and the platform it runs on, the enterprise engineering function, the technical strategy and reference architecture, and the production operations that keep released systems trusted. The role turns approved, requirements-backed use cases into secure, production-grade systems, agents, APIs, and integrations for every spoke, built once to a shared standard. Partners closely with enterprise AI strategy and leadership on use-case selection, prioritized roadmaps, enterprise architecture, to ensure the right systems and technical foundation.

Owns the AI technical strategy and reference architecture. Sets how AI systems are engineered: the reference architecture, integration patterns, agent platform, and build-versus-reuse calls that keep the portfolio coherent, built on McKinstry’s Filesystem-Driven Agent Architecture. Enterprise strategy and portfolio selection sit with leadership; this role owns the technical strategy that executes them.
Owns the AI platform and the agent harness. Builds and operates McKinstry’s core AI platform: the agent harness that turns a model into a governed capability (provider gateway, routing, context, memory, tool execution, output validation, and instrumentation), implemented on the Filesystem-Driven Agent Architecture, where every agent, skill, tool, and hook is defined in version-controlled files and folder location determines what is live. This is the platform the whole program builds on.
Owns the model-agnostic strategy and leads the build, buy, or host decision-making process. Keeps McKinstry portable across model providers through a provider-gateway layer, so changing a model or vendor is a configuration change, not a rebuild, with cost-tier routing and automatic failover. Owns the technical call on when to run managed models (Claude and peers), when to host models inside McKinstry’s own tenant for data sovereignty or cost, and when to fine-tune or stand up an in-house or open-source model. Integrates and operates the selected platforms and partners (Anthropic, Microsoft, cloud providers) to McKinstry standards, including evaluation, support escalation, and capacity management. Commercial terms and vendor strategy sit with leadership.
Owns the enterprise AI engineering function and standards. Runs the shared production build capability that serves every spoke, and sets the engineering standards, code-quality bar, and agent build-and-evaluation methodology, so systems are built once to a known standard instead of re-solved division by division.
Owns the AI marketplace. Owns the build and operation of the enterprise agent marketplace (McKinstry Labs): the catalog of approved, tested, reusable agents, skills, and tools that divisions discover and build on, so capability compounds across the company instead of being rebuilt spoke by spoke.
Chairs the architecture and production-readiness reviews. Owns the technical gate: nothing reaches production without passing it. A fully technical authority, separate from the strategy and governance chairs.
Engineers approved work into shipped systems. Takes the prioritized scope set by the domain directors and their product managers and engineers it into production: design, build, test, deploy, and the move from prototype to production-grade system. Owns delivery commitments and timelines. Every build starts from agreed requirements with a named business owner and is validated with end users.
Builds and leads the engineering team. Recruits, develops, and directs the AI, ML, software, and platform management and engineers; allocates capacity against agreed priorities. Accountable for throughput, quality, and the cost, risk, and value of what ships from experiment through sunset.
Owns production operations and the agent lifecycle. Runs deployment, monitoring, observability, LLMOps, versioning, and lifecycle management in production, including the evaluation harness and release gates that keep systems accurate and safe.
Owns the AI technology radar. Runs structured evaluations of emerging models, tools, and platforms and sets the program’s default technical position; escalates cross-division, client-facing, or spend-bearing calls for ratification.
Engineers security and responsible-AI controls into the build. Works with Information Security to build data protection, access control, model-access governance, prompt-injection defense, and output validation into the system, so guardrails live in code, not just policy. Implements the controls that satisfy RLSC and Data Governance policy.
Builds on the enterprise data foundation, not around it. Works with the Enterprise Data & AI Architect so every system reads and writes against the Four IDs and the MDM spine, and integrates into McKinstry systems such as Procore, Dynamics, and Fabric rather than standing up disconnected stores.

What You Need To Succeed At McKinstry

15+ years in software engineering, with hands-on experience shipping and operating production systems, and enough recent depth to set the technical bar, not only manage to it.
Demonstrated experience building and operating AI or ML applications in production (LLM applications, agents, RAG, evaluation, tool and function calling, multi-agent orchestration) as the person accountable for whether the system worked.
Platform depth: has built or operated an agent harness or runtime and a provider-abstraction layer, with sound judgment on managed, self-hosted, and open-source model tradeoffs across cost, latency, and data sovereignty.
Experience managing a team of 5+ direct reports, or 10+ including matrixed contributors, owning hiring, budget, and a delivery culture that balances exploration with production commitments.
Architecture judgment: can set a reference architecture and integration patterns for a portfolio of systems and hold teams and vendors to them, while building against an enterprise data layer owned elsewhere.
Fluent in modern cloud and AI delivery engineering (for example Azure, APIs, CI/CD, LLMOps, observability), able to integrate against enterprise systems and a master-data layer rather than building disconnected stores.
Can translate product requirements and data constraints into a build plan engineers execute, and validate the result with end users.
Security-by-design discipline: builds access control, data residency, model-access governance, prompt-injection defense, and output validation into the system rather than bolting them on later.
Strong written and verbal communication: can write a technical design an engineer builds from, and report engineering status and risk to executives without rework.
Comfortable owning the build, the platform, the technical strategy, and the solution architecture without owning enterprise strategy or product, engineering the right thing on a data spine owned elsewhere.
Bachelor’s degree in computer science, engineering, or a related field; relevant experience may be substituted. Cloud or security engineering credentials preferred.

Planned Parenthood organizations serve all people with care and compassion, with respect, and without judgment, striving to create equitable access to health care. Through health centers, programs in schools and communities, and online resources, Planned Parenthood is a trusted source of reliable education and information that allows people to make informed health decisions. We do all this because we care passionately about helping people lead healthier lives.

Planned Parenthood Federation of America (PPFA) is a 501(c)(3) charitable organization that supports the independently incorporated Planned Parenthood affiliates, which operate non-profit health centers across the U.S. PPFA also works to educate the public on and advocate for issues of sexual and reproductive health. Formed as the advocacy and political arm of Planned Parenthood Federation of America, Planned Parenthood Action Fund is a separate non-profit membership organization tax-exempt under section 501(c)(4). The Action Fund engages in educational, advocacy, and limited electoral activity, including grassroots organizing, legislative advocacy, and voter education in furtherance of the Planned Parenthood mission.

Planned Parenthood Federation of America (PPFA) and Planned Parenthood Action Fund seeks a dynamic and effective Director, Development Operations Infrastructure Engineering. This job reports directly to the Senior Director of Development Operations and Infrastructure in the IT Ops department of PPFA. The IT Ops department implements the architectural and infrastructural components used by PPFA, and is critical to the success of Planned Parenthood, its patients, supporters, donors, and staff.

jobs.description:
About Us

Rivian and Volkswagen Group Technologies is a joint venture between two industry leaders with a clear vision for automotive’s next chapter. From operating systems to zonal controllers to cloud and connectivity solutions, we’re addressing the challenges of electric vehicles through technology that will set the standards for software-defined vehicles around the world.

The road to the future is uncharted. By combining our expertise across connectivity, AI, security and more, we’ll map a new way forward. Working together, we’ll create a future that’s more connected, more intelligent, more sustainable for everyone.

Role Summary

We are looking for a Director of Data to own our data strategy and platform as we scale toward software-defined vehicles.

This is a hands-on leadership role where you'll set technical direction and stay close to the architecture and code, while building and managing a high-performing team responsible for high-volume, high-velocity vehicle and enterprise data.

You'll bring both the technical depth to make sound platform decisions and the people leadership to grow and run a team operating at scale.

We're hiring for this role in Palo Alto, Irvine, or Vancouver. We are happy to work with whichever location suits you best.

Responsibilities

Define and drive the data strategy and roadmap across vehicle telemetry, manufacturing, and enterprise data domains, aligning with engineering, product, and business stakeholders.
Own architecture decisions for large-scale data platforms (ingestion, storage, processing, and serving layers) handling high-volume streaming and batch data.
Stay hands-on: review designs and code, dive into pipeline or performance issues, and set technical standards by example, not just by policy.
Recruit, manage, mentor, and grow a team of data engineers and analytics professionals; own hiring plans, performance management, and career development.
Partner with quality, manufacturing, product, and software engineering teams to ensure data infrastructure supports reliability, safety, and product analytics needs.
Establish data governance, quality, and security standards across pipelines and platforms, ensuring compliance with relevant regulatory and privacy requirements.
Build and maintain stakeholder-facing reporting on platform health, data quality, and delivery against roadmap commitments.
Evaluate and integrate modern tooling (e.g., Databricks, Spark, Kafka, cloud data warehouses, AI/LLM-assisted engineering tools) to keep the platform and team ahead of scale demands.
Manage budget, vendor, and tooling decisions for the data organization.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications:

8–10 years of overall industry experience in data engineering or analytics, including 3+ years managing high-volume data engineering or analytics teams.
Demonstrated hands-on technical depth in building and operating large-scale data systems, proficiency in SQL and Python required, along with hands-on experience with Databricks required (additional experience with Spark or equivalent distributed data platforms a plus).
Track record of designing and scaling data architecture (ingestion, ETL/ELT, streaming, and storage) for high-volume, high-velocity data.
Experience hiring, developing, and retaining data engineering talent, with a demonstrated ability to balance IC-level technical involvement with people leadership.
Strong cross-functional partnership skills and being comfortable working with engineering, product, quality, and manufacturing stakeholders to translate business needs into data infrastructure.
Experience establishing data governance, quality, and security practices at an organizational level.
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Data Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical discipline; advanced degree a plus.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in automotive, mobility, IoT, or another industry with high-volume sensor/telemetry data.
Experience integrating or prompting AI/LLM tools into engineering workflows.
Familiarity with dashboard/BI tooling (HEX, Tableau, Power BI, or similar) for stakeholder reporting.

About The Role

We're hiring a Director of Engineering to own the Shopify platform that runs ritual.com. This is bigger than the storefront: Shopify is the commercial operating system of our business, and this role owns it end to end—catalog and store configuration, the app stack, subscription commerce, and the integrations that connect the store to fulfillment, operations, finance, and marketing.

You'll lead our in-house engineering and QA team, own the technical roadmap for the platform in partnership with product, and represent engineering with senior stakeholders across the company. Critically, this role sits at the intersection of every team that plugs into the Shopify platform: growth and retention marketing (pixels, conversion tracking, catalog syncing, lifecycle and CRM integrations), customer support (helpdesk and customer data tooling), supply chain and logistics (fulfillment, order and inventory flows), and accounting (revenue recognition and finance data). Own the Shopify platform end to end, including catalog setup and product data architecture, store settings, markets and checkout configuration, and overall store health. Establish clear, scalable platform standards and help the broader team understand how and why the Shopify instance is configured.
Lead subscription commerce configuration through Recharge, overseeing plans and pricing, discount logic, customer portal experiences, and the connections between subscriptions, promotions, and international markets.
Build, maintain, and evolve integrations connecting Shopify with critical business systems, including supply chain and logistics platforms, fulfillment, order and inventory synchronization, accounting and revenue recognition workflows, webhooks, APIs, and custom applications.

Guide Shopify theme development by partnering with an experienced engineering team with strong Liquid expertise. Collaborate with digital product management and web design to bring new features and experiences to life, while contributing to code reviews and fostering a high standard for performance, accessibility, maintainability, and polish.

Partner closely with growth and retention marketing as a technical leader, overseeing the implementation and health of marketing pixels and conversion tracking, product catalog synchronization with advertising platforms, lifecycle and CRM integrations, and the data flows that support them. Help teams identify and execute effective technical solutions that support growth and retention goals.
Connect teams across the business through the platform, partnering with customer support, CRM, supply chain and logistics, accounting, and other stakeholders who rely on Shopify and its surrounding systems. Help ensure customer, order, subscription, and financial data flows reliably to the teams that need it, while representing cross-functional needs in engineering planning and roadmap discussions.
Champion web accessibility for ritual.com, helping maintain the storefront in alignment with WCAG 2.1 AA standards. Embed accessibility into design reviews and definitions of done, and coordinate the annual manual accessibility audit with an external partner—from planning and triage through remediation and follow-through in the sprint cycle.
Help lead an AI-native development practice, using modern AI development tools such as Cursor and Linear to support thoughtful, efficient delivery. Establish team practices for using AI-assisted development responsibly, including standards for code quality, review, testing, security, and safe deployment.
Facilitate the team's sprint cycles from planning through delivery, helping groom and scope work, manage capacity, clarify priorities, and foster accountability across engineering and cross-functional partners contributing to the roadmap. Create the conditions for teams to deliver high-quality work predictably and sustainably.
Lead, hire, and develop the engineering and QA organization, supporting an in-house team of front-end engineers and a QA function led by a Senior QA Manager. Foster a collaborative, inclusive team culture and take shared ownership of quality and delivery across the full lifecycle, from planning and development through testing and release.
Build and manage strong vendor and partner relationships across the platform ecosystem, including app providers, agencies, and audit partners. Oversee budgets and contracts, set clear expectations, and create productive partnerships focused on measurable outcomes and long-term value.

Clear Communicator: You express ideas clearly and thoughtfully—whether in writing, speaking, or storytelling. You tailor messages to your audience and make complex concepts easy to understand.
Empowered Collaborator: You work across teams with trust and respect. You challenge ideas constructively, co-create solutions, and move projects forward through collective effort.

Detail-Oriented: You care about the details—because you know they add up to better, more trustworthy outcomes.

Technical Acumen: You bring deep engineering knowledge and apply it to real-world challenges.

What You'll Need

8+ years of software engineering experience, including 4+ years of deep Shopify platform experience spanning administration and development: catalog and product data architecture, store and checkout configuration, markets, and app stack management for a high-volume brand.
Proven back-end/platform ownership: fluency with the Shopify Admin and Storefront APIs, webhooks, and app extensions, and hands-on experience building and maintaining custom Shopify apps and integrations that stay reliable over time.
Experience integrating Shopify with operational and financial systems.

Comfort operating as the technical hub for many non-technical teams at once—marketing, customer support, supply chain, accounting—translating between business goals and technical constraints, and managing competing integration needs without losing platform coherence.
5+ years of engineering management experience—you know how to hire, set expectations, review work, develop engineers, and hold a quality bar across a team, and you've owned delivery outcomes at the team level, not just the ticket level.

About Varda

Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules. Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses.

From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind.

Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital.

Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL.

Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem.

About This Role

As Director, Mechanisms Engineering - Pharmaceutical Payloads at Varda, you will build and lead the team responsible for Varda's in-orbit pharmaceutical manufacturing payloads—the core of Varda's commercial business. This role combines deep technical authority with team leadership, product definition, and development execution responsibility. You will own the successful development and flight of precision electromechanical fluid-handling systems that process and crystallize pharmaceutical compounds in microgravity—then survive hypersonic reentry and return to Earth for product recovery and hardware iteration. The payloads your team designs, builds, and flies will directly determine whether in-space pharmaceutical manufacturing becomes a commercial reality.

You will build and grow a team of payload engineers responsible for individual pharmaceutical payload missions while also owning the technical definition and evolution of Varda's pharma payload product line. This includes defining the system architecture, fluid system design philosophy, and development approach, and establishing the engineering standards and processes that enable reliable execution as Varda scales in both cadence and scope.

You'll expand Varda's pharmaceutical payload capability to a scaled, repeatable product line—building the team, technical standards, and development processes to get there.

This role is ideal for a technically exceptional leader who wants to build an elite team and own the first ever industrial manufacturing capability in space from strategy through execution.

Build and lead a team of payload engineers, each responsible for executing individual pharmaceutical payload missions

Own pharmaceutical payload engineering execution against company goals and customer contracts, including schedule, cost, and technical performance

Define and maintain standards for payload design, analysis, integration, testing, mission execution, documentation, and project management

Standardize processes for environmental test campaigns, mission operations, post-flight hardware inspection, and anomaly resolution
Drive continuous improvement through lessons learned and feedback from flight programs

Breadth across at least two adjacent hardware disciplines (e.g., avionics, mechanisms, software, structures, thermal, optics, test, etc.)
Demonstrated ability to set technical direction and deliver results through other engineers
Track record managing multiple concurrent engineering development efforts
Experience establishing and enforcing technical and programmatic standards across teams
Exceptional communication ability with diverse technical and executive audiences

Experience building, scaling, or managing hardware engineering teams
Experience owning technical roadmaps or standardized hardware product offerings
Experience developing or operating hardware for pharmaceutical, bioprocess, or sterile/cleanroom manufacturing applications

Familiarity with cGMP principles or regulated hardware environments
Significant experience planning and executing environmental testing (vibration, TVAC, EMI/EMC)

Mentor and develop your team

jobs.description:
Job Description

Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) is continuing its rapid expansion across parts of North America, delivering next-generation cloud infrastructure to support enterprise and AI-driven workloads. As our cloud footprint continues to grow, we are seeking an accomplished executive to lead Cloud Hardware Support (CHS) across parts of North America.

This Senior Director will provide strategic and operational leadership for a rapidly growing regional organization, with responsibility spanning Build & Deployment, steady-state operations, hardware maintenance, and break-fix support across Oracle's cloud infrastructure.

The successful candidate will establish a scalable operating model that enables rapid regional expansion while maintaining operational excellence, customer service, and workforce effectiveness. This leader will build high-performing teams, standardize operations across multiple countries, and drive continuous improvement through automation, AI, process engineering, and operational innovation.

This is a unique opportunity to shape the future of Oracle's cloud operations across one of its fastest-growing regions.

Responsibilities

Key Responsibilities

We are seeking a dynamic and visionary executive with a proven track record of leading hyperscale infrastructure organizations through periods of rapid growth and transformation. This leader will be responsible for scaling Cloud Hardware Support operations across parts of North America while ensuring the organization remains operationally efficient, customer-focused, and ready to support Oracle's continued cloud expansion.

Additional responsibilities include:

Provide executive leadership for Cloud Hardware Support operations across parts of North America, including Build & Deployment, production readiness, hardware lifecycle management, and break-fix operations.
Develop and execute a scalable regional operating model capable of supporting continued hyperscale growth across multiple countries.
Lead a large, geographically dispersed organization that is expected to grow significantly as Oracle expands its cloud footprint throughout the region.
Drive operational excellence by standardizing deployment methodologies, improving service delivery, and implementing best practices across all regional operations.
Champion the use of AI, automation, process engineering, and data-driven decision making to improve productivity, increase operational efficiency, and reduce the dependency between infrastructure growth and headcount expansion.
Build and develop high-performing leadership teams while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement.
Partner closely with Engineering, Networking, Software Development, Product, Supply Chain, Data Center Engineering, and other cross-functional organizations to ensure successful delivery of new cloud regions and ongoing operational excellence.
Establish strong contractor, partner, and vendor relationships to support regional deployment and operational readiness.
Ensure customer commitments and operational service levels are consistently achieved while proactively managing operational risk.
Act as the senior Cloud Hardware Support leader across parts of North America, influencing strategic priorities and representing the organization with executive stakeholders across Oracle.

Preferred Skills And Experience

Executive leadership experience within hyperscale cloud infrastructure, cloud operations, hardware support, data center operations, or infrastructure engineering.
Proven experience leading large, geographically distributed organizations across multiple countries and cultures.
Demonstrated success scaling operations within rapidly growing cloud or technology organizations.

This position is in CMSD (Configurable Mixed-Signal Division), which is part of Renesas’ Analog & Mixed-Signal Product Group. The CMSD team is continuously expanding the product portfolio that includes high-performance analog IP’s, DC-DC converters, and FPGA solutions.

As a Senior Manager Analog Engineering you will lead a team of analog designers and be the technical project lead for the development of our configurable mixed-signal ASICs. You will be responsible for all technical aspects of the project, from the initial concept phase through definition and architecture selection to design development, verification, and collaboration with cross-functional teams (test development, qualification etc.) to prepare the product for market release.

Work with the product definition and marketing team to develop a specification that gives the product a competitive advantage in the IC market
Develop the product’s system architecture to optimize performance, power, and die size
Specify the requirements of individual IPs used in the product

Lead a high-quality product development by ensuring that best practices are followed, through thorough peer reviews, and detailed documentation
Collaborate with cross-functional teams on test development, product engineering, bench evaluation, and quality assurance
Mentor and develop your team

MSEE + 15 years of experience in analog and mixed-signal design
Fully competent in all common aspects of analog design
Design experience in precision analog circuitry
Design experience in power management circuits and high voltage circuitry (BCD processes)
Ability to develop system architectures
Knowledge of analog circuit modeling and AMS simulations
Knowledge of all aspects of IC development beyond analog design to efficiently collaborate with cross-functional teams: understanding the basic digital design flow, packaging, test engineering, quality assurance, and product engineering
Ability to see the big picture while not losing track of details
